questions.question: Which definition best describes the design metric “Unit Cost” as presented in the context?

options.A: The one‑time monetary expense for research and development of the system.
options.B: The monetary cost of manufacturing each copy of the system, excluding NRE cost.
options.C: The physical space required by the system.
options.D: The amount of power the system consumes during operation.

questions.explanation:
“Unit cost: the monetary cost of manufacturing each copy of the system, excluding NRE cost” is stated on page 30 and reiterated on page 33.  

---

questions.question: According to the provided material, how is “NRE Cost” defined?

options.A: The cost of producing one unit of the product.
options.B: The ongoing expense of power consumption over the device’s lifetime.
options.C: The one‑time monetary cost of designing the system such as research, firmware, and UI development.
options.D: The cost associated with the physical size of the device.

questions.explanation:
The context defines NRE cost as “The one‑time monetary cost of designing the system such as Research cost” on page 30.  

---

questions.question: In the smart watch case study, which statement accurately defines the design metric “Size”?

options.A: The amount of battery life the watch can provide.
options.B: The physical space required by the system, needing to be compact and lightweight.
options.C: The monetary cost of each watch unit.
options.D: The speed at which the processor can execute instructions.

questions.explanation:
Page 33 lists “Size: Must be very compact and lightweight,” and page 30 describes size as “the physical space required by the system.”  

---

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the definition of the design metric “Performance” for the smart watch?

options.A: Real‑time heart‑rate reading, smooth UI, and fast Bluetooth connection.
options.B: The total cost of research, engineering, and tooling.
options.C: The number of days the battery can last on a single charge.
options.D: The flexibility to add new applications after release.

questions.explanation:
Page 33 details performance as “Real‑time heart rate reading, smooth UI, fast BT connection.”  

---

questions.question: How does the context define the design metric “Power” for the smart watch?

options.A: The monetary cost of producing each watch.
options.B: The need for the device to operate for 1–7 days on a small battery.
options.C: The ability to modify the system after release.
options.D: The time required to build a working prototype.

questions.explanation:
Page 33 states “Power: Must run for 1–7 days on a small battery.”  

---

questions.question: Which description correctly defines “Flexibility” as a design metric in the smart watch evaluation?

options.A: The ability to support new apps and updates after the product is released.
options.B: The monetary expense of the unit’s components.
options.C: The physical dimensions of the device.
options.D: The time needed to bring the product to market.

questions.explanation:
Page 34 notes that the watch “Should support new apps & updates,” reflecting flexibility.  

---

questions.question: According to the provided material, what is the definition of “Time‑to‑prototype”?

options.A: The duration needed to manufacture the final product at scale.
options.B: The time needed to build a working version of the system.
options.C: The period required to achieve full market release.
options.D: The interval between successive firmware updates.

questions.explanation:
Page 31 defines “Time‑to‑prototype: the time needed to build a working version of the system.”  

---

questions.question: Which statement best defines “Time‑to‑market” as described in the context?

options.A: The length of time required to develop a system to the point it can be released and sold to customers.
options.B: The time it takes for a battery to deplete under normal use.
options.C: The period needed to design the user interface only.
options.D: The duration of the manufacturing process for each unit.

questions.explanation:
Page 31 explains “Time‑to‑market: the time required to develop a system … to be released and sold to customers.”  

---

questions.question: How is “Maintainability” defined in the context of design metrics?

options.A: The ability of the system to operate without any power consumption.
options.B: The capacity to modify the system after its initial release.
options.C: The cost associated with non‑recurring engineering.
options.D: The size of the device’s physical enclosure.

questions.explanation:
Page 31 lists “Maintainability: the ability to modify the system after its initial release.”  

---

questions.question: Which definition aligns with the design metric “Correctness” as mentioned in the provided excerpt?

options.A: The measure of how accurately the system performs its intended functions.
options.B: The total monetary cost of producing each unit.
options.C: The flexibility to add new features post‑deployment.
options.D: The speed at which the processor executes instructions.

questions.explanation: Page 31 includes “Correctness, safety, many more” among design metrics, implying correctness refers to the system performing its intended functions accurately.
